help.intro: The closing conversation of this module, run in your own AI assistant with voice mode on: a seven-minute chat about you — name, where you live and come from, your family, and the numbers and colours around you. Copy the exercise, paste it in, say 'Los geht's', and answer in full sentences. The tutor will not interrupt to correct you; it keeps every correction for the report at the end, together with a score you bring back here. This is as close to a real first conversation as practice gets: someone asking, you answering in whole sentences, with the verb endings and sein/haben forms carrying the meaning.
help.tips[0].title: Answer the question that was asked, in a full sentence
help.tips[0].text: Woher kommst du? → Ich komme aus … (not 'Aus Spanien'). Wie alt bist du? → Ich bin … Jahre alt. Match the verb in the question.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Do you have siblings? – Yes, I have a brother.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Where do you live? – I live in Lyon.
help.tips[0].check.q: Woher kommst du? Pick the full-sentence answer to this question.
help.tips[0].check.why: The question uses kommst, so you answer with the matching ich komme aus … in a full sentence.
help.tips[0].visual.moves[0].label: Who you are
help.tips[0].visual.moves[1].label: Where from, where now
help.tips[0].visual.moves[3].label: Ask back
help.tips[1].title: Use what this level gave you
help.tips[1].text: sein and haben, the -e / -st / -t endings, der/die/das, numbers to 100, colours: the tutor listens for exactly these.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: My car is blue. I have two cats. They are black.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: My brother is twenty and lives in Vienna.
help.tips[1].check.why: Meine Katzen are 'they', and sein for sie (plural) is sind.
help.tips[2].title: Ask back
help.tips[2].text: Und du? / Und Sie? turns an answer into a conversation and buys you a second to think.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: I have two siblings. And you?
help.tips[2].check.why: Und du? hands the question back: 'And you?'
help.remember[0]: Whole sentences only — the score is on the sentence, not the word.
help.remember[1]: Keep talking through mistakes; the corrections come at the end.
help.exam: A short conversation about yourself and your family is the heart of the A1 speaking exam — and of every first chat with a neighbour.
help.hook: Hold a five-minute chat about yourself in German: your name, home, family, and the numbers and colours around you.
speaking.topic: Introducing myself: my name, where I live, where I come from, my family, numbers and colours around me.
